title: Next contract under-states the cost of the command it names: it counts error blocks only and ignores advisory pairs and consensus
where: source/cli/src/cli/check-render-views.ts:200 (isFill requires severity==='error'), :309 fillStep, :347 fills = errors.filter(isFill); docs/cli-reference.md:366
evidence: The docs say `cost` is the cost of running `command`, "the whole command, never one block's share of it" (cli-reference.md:366). Scratch project $TMPDIR/consist-c has 1 enforced prose pair, 2 advisory prose pairs, 1 stale script pair and 1 advisory script pair not yet run, with consensus 3. `yg check` prints `next: yg check --approve --only-deterministic  (unverified — 1 script pair · free)` and `then: yg check --approve  (1 reviewer pair · paid — ask the user to approve it first)`. The JSON gives next.cost {free:1, reviewerPairs:0}. The same tree under `yg check --approve --dry-run` prints `fill  5 pairs · 2 script (free) · 9 reviewer calls (consensus included)`, listing 3 reviewer pairs. So the paid step is announced as 1 pair when it bills 3 pairs and 9 calls, and the free step is announced as 1 pair when it fills 2. It happens because `--approve` fills every unverified pair, advisory included (prime:81), while isFill counts only error blocks. Consensus is invisible in check's own units: check counts pairs, while dry-run and impact count calls. This is a follow-on to readiness M6 (issue 228). That issue fixed free-vs-paid but not scope.
proposal: Work out FillStep from every unverified, non-draft pair the named command would fill, whatever its severity. For `--only-deterministic` that is the script pairs; for `--approve` it is all of them. Take the counts from the pairs[] data (kind plus verdict), which the dry run classifies the same way. State reviewer cost as pairs and calls (`3 reviewer pairs · 9 calls · paid`), and add `reviewerCalls` to next.cost as an additive field. Keep `remaining` as it is, because it counts errors by design. Cost: roughly 1 day, touching check-render-views.ts plus tests. Verified when an e2e test asserts, on 3 fixtures (script-only, mixed, advisory-only), that `yg check --json`.next.cost matches `yg check --approve --dry-run --json`.dryRunBudget for the same tree.

v.reason: I re-ran it on $TMPDIR/consist-c. `yg check` prints `then: yg check --approve  (1 reviewer pair · paid …)` and JSON next.cost {free:1, reviewerPairs:0}. `--approve --dry-run` on the same tree lists 3 reviewer pairs (9 calls) and 2 script pairs. The cause is in the code: isFill (check-render-views.ts:200) requires severity==='error', and fillStep sums only those blocks, while prime:81 says --approve fills every unverified pair. Issue 228 fixed free vs paid but not scope, so this is not filed. The proposal is sound, and the parity test against dryRunBudget is a good acceptance check.

title: The agent protocol contradicts the CLI on paid fills and on the next line: prime says run --approve unprompted, the CLI says ask the user first; other commands name the paid fill without asking
where: yg prime (live) lines 7, 189, 193, 230; docs/glossary.md:203-205 (approval); check-render-views.ts:375 (repeatsFix); cli/aspects.ts health footer; formatters/context-node.ts next/then
evidence: Prime line 7 says: "A `yg check` report ends with a `next:` line — the one concrete step to take first." In reality, $TMPDIR/consist-b (1 error block, 4 warning blocks) prints no `next:` line at all. That behaviour is documented only in cli-reference.md:544 and knowledge cli-reference:87, and the code is `repeatsFix = pool.length === 1 && …`. Prime line 189 says "run `yg check --approve` exactly ONCE at the end … Do not defer it." Line 193 says "resolve every unverified pair". Line 230 lists what needs the user's signature (suppress, architecture, status, review_by, advise) and leaves out paid fills. The glossary's "approval" entry leaves them out too. The CLI meanwhile prints `yg check --approve  (… · paid — ask the user to approve it first)` with requiresUser:true, and cli-reference.md:366 says a paid fill needs the user's approval before it runs. Other commands skip the contract entirely. `yg aspects --health` ends `next: yg check --approve` with 3 reviewer pairs pending. `yg context --node cart` ends `then: yg check --approve`. `yg impact --aspect prose-adv` says "then run yg check --approve". None of these carries a cost or an ask.
proposal: This needs Krzysztof's ruling: does an agent need consent before a paid fill? The CLI already assumes yes, and the 6.1.0 ruling that Yggdrasil's reviewer is the one judge makes it the only judge. Encode the ruling once, in the glossary entry "approval" and prime lines 189, 193 and 230. Replace line 7 with the documented rule ("when there is one error block, its fix is the step"). Export fillStep and its cost wording from check-render-views, and have context, health and impact use them instead of hand-written `next: yg check --approve`. Cost: about half a day of text plus a small refactor. Verified by a test that scans every `next:`/`then:` a command prints: any `yg check --approve` without `--only-deterministic` must carry the paid annotation whenever reviewer pairs are pending. A prime test should also assert that the rule about the missing next line is present.

Prime:189 says to run --approve 'exactly ONCE at the end', and prime:230's list of things needing the user's signature leaves out paid fills. The CLI meanwhile prints 'paid — ask the user to approve it first'. `aspects --health` prints a bare `next: yg check --approve`, `context --node cart` prints `then: yg check --approve`, and impact says 'then run yg check --approve'; none carries a cost. decisions.md has no ruling on consent for paid fills. title: Next derives its target by parsing the fix prose: one unmapped file gives 'edit src/orphan.ts' (the wrong file), several give the whole sentence
where: source/cli/src/cli/check-render-views.ts:158 namedFile, :248-255 verb/namedFile path in blockAction; unmapped fix text in core/check-coverage-phase.ts
evidence: In $TMPDIR/consist-a and $TMPDIR/consist-i, with one unmapped file in coverage.required, the output is `next: edit src/orphan.ts  (unmapped)`, and the JSON has next.target.file = "src/orphan.ts" and command null. Renaming the file gives `next: edit src/zz.ts`. The fix, however, is to edit a yg-node.yaml mapping or create a node. The block's own fix says "Add each file to a node's mapping…", and prime:195 agrees. With four unmapped files, the same code gives `next: Add each file to a node's mapping, or create a new node for it — yg context --file src/o1.ts lists candidate owners  (unmapped)`, which is a sentence rather than a step. blockAction runs regexes over English: a leading verb (`/^(?:fix|edit|…|add|…)/`) followed by the first path-like token. So a wording change moves the step, which is the fragility CLI-comm M9 described. It was not removed; it moved into the renderer.
proposal: Have emitters supply the step as data. The Diagnostic model already has `fix.command` (output-diagnostic.ts:30). Give IssueMessage an optional `step: {command?, target?, verb}` field, set by the module that knows the remedy. For unmapped files that is `yg context --file <first>` (read-only, lists candidate owners) with target kind `mapping`. Remove namedFile and the verb heuristic once every T1/T2 code sets a step. Cost: about 1-2 days, mostly per-code audit. Verified by a table test over every registered code: the fixture's next.command either runs (`--help`-parseable) or next.target names a graph file, never a source file for coverage codes.

v.reason: Reproduced: consist-a gives `next: edit src/orphan.ts  (unmapped)` and consist-i gives `next: edit src/zz.ts`. The code path is blockAction: the leading-verb regex matches 'Add', then namedFile takes the first path-like token, check-render-views.ts:158 and :248-255. For the most common adoption error, the headline step points at the wrong file. The full per-code step model costs M. A cheaper stopgap exists: for coverage codes, emit `yg context --file <first>` as the step.

title: Status semantics differ between the glossary, prime and knowledge: who sets it, whether advisory can block, whether status is 'rendering only'
where: docs/glossary.md:73 and :85 (from templates/portal/js/glossary.js); yg prime lines 25, 71, 109; yg knowledge read aspect-status (lines 3-12, 'Declaration sites'); docs/aspect-status.md:41-46
evidence: The glossary says status is "set by `status:` in the rule's own file". Knowledge aspect-status lists six declaration sites (node own/cascade, type, flow, port, plus implies status_inherit) and a max() rule, and prime:71 says the same. The glossary says advisory refusals "never block", and prime:109 says "An advisory pair never blocks `yg check` — whether it is refused OR unverified". I tested this live on $TMPDIR/consist-d: advisory reviewer rule prose-adv with max_prompt_chars 1000 gives `error[prompt-too-large] 2 pairs in 2 nodes` and a FAIL header. Knowledge and aspect-status.md:41-46 document that exception; the glossary and prime do not. Prime:25 says status is "rendering only … except `draft`". Knowledge aspect-status says "it is NOT rendering only. Two further operational consequences follow from `enforced`": the script-refusal skip of reviewer pairs, which prime:81 itself describes, and positive closure. Glossary line 5 promises "Each word here has one meaning, the same in these docs, in `yg prime`, in `yg knowledge`, in the CLI output and in the portal."
proposal: Correct glossary.js. For status: "set on the rule (`status:`), raisable — never lowerable — at any attach site; effective status is the highest". For advisory: "… never block, except a pair whose prompt is too large to judge". Rewrite prime:25 and :109 to match the knowledge topic, which is the most precise text. Generate prime's status paragraph from the same glossary entries (glossary-sync.test already exists) so the two cannot drift again. Cost: a few hours. Verified by a test asserting that the prime and glossary status and advisory sentences are the same strings, and that prime contains "prompt-too-large" wherever it says advisory never blocks.

title: Retired vocabulary survives in the portal, CLI validator messages, JSON and knowledge topic names; the guard matches only 22 narrow phrases
where: source/cli/tests/unit/repo/no-retired-terms.test.ts:36-58; templates/portal/js/views/coverage-view.js:106-107, overview-view.js:260, rulebook-view.js:145, panel-aspect.js:86,91, js/bootstrap.js:128,146; core/checks/aspect-contracts.ts:131-151; formatters/context-node.ts:123, context-file.ts:143; cli/aspects.ts:1001; knowledge topic ids writing-llm-aspects / writing-deterministic-aspects
evidence: Seen live on $TMPDIR/consist-i: `error[aspect-unexpected-rule-source] Aspect 'adv-rule' has reviewer 'llm' but check.mjs is present`, with fix `… or change reviewer to 'deterministic'`. The glossary says a script rule "has no reviewer" and lists "deterministic reviewer" under "Not called". `yg context --node cart` on a draft script rule prints "(reviewer skipped; aspect is draft)". `yg aspects --health` says "exposure = times the reviewer judged" for script rules. The portal's strings contradict the glossary on the same surface the glossary is generated for. coverage-view has "of N LLM + M deterministic expected" and "(N deterministic, M LLM verified)". overview and rulebook say "green means a reviewer actually checked it and approved", which is false for script rules. The Approve dialog says "(N free deterministic)" and then "Approved · re-checked", while the glossary says `--approve` is not an approval. In JSON, yg-check/1 pairs carry `reviewer: "deterministic"` and `verdict: "approved"` next to a top-level `judges` array, and yg-aspects/1 uses `kind: llm|deterministic`. Issue 177 deliberately left JSON and codes unchanged, but the glossary never maps those tokens. None of these match the test's patterns, for example `\bdeterministic (aspect|rule)s?\b`.
proposal: (1) Add a 'machine token' line to each glossary entry: reviewer rule ↔ `llm`; script rule ↔ `deterministic` (`reviewer.type`, `--only-deterministic`, JSON `kind`); bundle ↔ `aggregate`; passed ↔ `approved`. The frozen /1 tokens are then explained rather than contradicted. (2) Fix the roughly 10 live strings listed above. (3) Widen the guard with `\bLLM\b` and bare `deterministic` in portal and CLI string literals, `reviewer '(llm|deterministic)'`, `change reviewer to`, and `approved` in prose, with an allowlist for flags and JSON keys. (4) Add knowledge aliases `writing-reviewer-rules` / `writing-script-rules` and keep the old ids resolving. Cost: about 1 day. Verified when the widened test is green, and when a grep of `yg portal --static` output for LLM/deterministic finds only token contexts.

title: The verdict/state taxonomy forks: 'stale' is a verdict in pairs[] and totals but a cause of 'unverified' in issues; 'stale' also means 'pruned'; infra failure is labelled 'Refused'
where: core/check-json.ts:267-273 (totals.verdicts), yg-check/1 pairs[].verdict; docs/cli-reference.md:312-322, :741; docs/the-lock.md:167; yg prime line 79 and 103; docs/glossary.md (no 'stale' entry)
evidence: In $TMPDIR/consist-a, `yg check --json` gives totals.verdicts {approved:2, unverified:2, stale:1}. There are 3 unverified findings, and the text heads all three `error[unverified]`/`warning[unverified]`. pairs[] gives emits-telemetry@payment `verdict: "stale"`, while the matching issue is code `unverified`, cause `stale`. A consumer summing totals.verdicts.unverified under-counts. Horde carries `verdicts` through node.mjs:692. In the fill, "pruned 3 stale verdicts" (the-lock.md:167, cli-reference.md:741) means verdicts no longer expected, which is a second meaning. Prime:79 heads an infrastructure failure "Refused (infrastructure — fail closed)" and then says the pair stays unverified. The glossary says refused means "the code broke the rule", and JSON reports that case as unverified with cause reviewer-failed. cli-reference.md:312-313 describes draftSkipped as "how many expected pairs a draft rule dropped (… a count of draft rules …)", which contradicts itself within one sentence.
proposal: Add glossary entries: "stale — an unverified pair whose verdict was recorded over inputs that have since changed (cause `stale`)" and "finding / block" (the units of the verdict line). In family-contracts and cli-reference, state that totals.verdicts.unverified excludes stale and that together they give the unverified pairs. Add an additive `totals.verdicts.unverifiedAll` if helpful. Rename the prune line to "pruned 3 verdicts no longer expected". Rename prime:79 to "Not judged (infrastructure — fail closed)". Fix the draftSkipped sentence. Cost: a few hours. Verified by a test asserting sum(totals.verdicts minus approved and refused) equals the number of pairs whose group code is unverified, on a mixed fixture.

title: 'Covered' counts excluded files: a fresh repo with 0 nodes reports 4/7 covered, the JSON split is nulled when type-level is off, and Horde works around it
where: core/check-coverage-phase.ts:137-145; core/check-json.ts:262-264 (nodeOwned/typeCovered/excluded null unless typeLevel); header renderer; docs/glossary.md:215-243; Horde skills/horde/scripts/node.mjs:680-686
evidence: A fresh `yg init --no-reviewer` with src/a.ts, README.md and package.json gives `yg check: PASS  1 warning   0 nodes · 4/7 files covered (4 excluded)`. The only covered files are Yggdrasil's own plumbing (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .clinerules, .gitattributes). The glossary defines covered as node-owned, type-covered or excluded, and in the same section says excluded means "Yggdrasil ignores it everywhere"; the headline ratio does not ignore it. With type_level off (examples/checkout-flow copy), the header reads `9/11 files covered`, with 5 of the 9 excluded and nothing saying so, and the JSON gives coverage {covered:9, nodeOwned:null, typeCovered:null, excluded:null}. Excluded is a config fact, independent of type-level. Horde's node.mjs:680 comment reads "coverage.covered also counts excluded files … covered is what a node or a type answers for". When the split is null, Horde falls back to the inflated `covered`.
proposal: Headline ratio: (nodeOwned + typeCovered) / (files − excluded), with excluded shown separately: `0/3 files covered · 4 excluded`. Always emit nodeOwned, typeCovered (0 when off) and excluded in yg-check/1. That is additive, since it replaces null with numbers, and it lets Horde drop its fallback. Keep `coverage.covered` in JSON with its current meaning, documented as "accounted for", or add `ownedOrTyped` alongside. Cost: about half a day plus a Horde follow-up. Verified when a fresh init prints 0/N covered, and when Horde's quality-index test passes without the null branch.

v.reason: Reproduced: a fresh `yg init --no-reviewer` with src/a.ts, README.md and package.json prints `0 nodes · 4/7 files covered (4 excluded)`. All 4 covered files are excluded Yggdrasil plumbing. check-json.ts:262-264 nulls nodeOwned, typeCovered and excluded unless typeLevel is on. Horde node.mjs:680-686 carries an explicit workaround comment. The headline is misleading, and the proposal is additive and sound.

title: Duplicated logic that has already diverged: two Next engines, two dead-rule checks under different codes on check and advise, and seven wordings for 'unknown rule id'
where: core/check-suggested-next.ts (283 lines; called at core/check.ts:506, cli/check.ts:144, core/fill-report.ts:248) vs cli/check-render-views.ts computeNext (overwrites it at :555); core/checks/aspects.ts:287 orphaned-aspect vs core/checks/aspect-contracts.ts:390 aspect-effective-nowhere vs core/advise-nominations.ts:1051 dead-attach; aspect-not-found paths in impact, aspect-test, simulate, aspects-log, drill, drill-add, check
evidence: (a) result.suggestedNext is computed by the old engine up to three times per run. enrichCheckJson then replaces it with computeNext's text (check-render-views.ts:555), so the old engine only still exists to drift. (b) One dead rule (prose-rule, attached nowhere, in $TMPDIR/consist-b) produces two warnings in `yg check`: `warning[aspect-effective-nowhere]` and `warning[orphaned-aspect]`. It also produces two nominations in `yg advise`: `nomination[dead-attach]` (the same text under a different code) and `nomination[orphaned-aspect]`. The advise versions append "— ask the user to approve it first" to "Check the attach sites". (c) An unknown rule id gives: `error[aspect-not-found]: Unknown aspect 'nope'` (check, whose why still says "--aspect drills into ONE rule", the retired "drill into"); `error[command-error]: Aspect not found: nope` (impact); `Aspect 'nope' not found.` (aspect-test); `Candidate rule 'nope' was not found.` (simulate); `No rule 'nope' in this graph.` (aspects log add/read, drill add); and `yg drill requires an aspect declared in .yggdrasil/aspects/ (got 'nope').` (drill). That is 6 wordings and 2 codes. `node-not-found`, by contrast, gives one `what` and one `next: yg find` across node, impact, context and log. (d) The advise code `uncovered-hot-spot` names a mapped node, and advise-nominations.ts:782 says draft-only nodes "count as uncovered". The glossary reserves "covered" for mapping and "unguarded" for no rule.
proposal: Delete check-suggested-next.ts and set suggestedNext only in the renderer. Suppress orphaned-aspect when the aspect has a rule source, since effective-nowhere subsumes it (keep it for bundles). Make advise reuse the check code (`aspect-effective-nowhere`). Add a shared `aspectNotFound(id, why)` diagnostic, the twin of the node-not-found one, with next `yg aspects`. Rename `uncovered-hot-spot` to `unguarded-hot-spot`, keeping the old id as an alias in `--ids` and dismiss records. Cost: about 1 day. Verified by a test that runs all 7 commands with an unknown id and asserts one code and one `what`, a test that a dead rule yields exactly one finding per surface, and a repo guard that core/check-suggested-next.ts is gone.

title: The trust model disagrees with itself: the table omits yg simulate, which executes check.mjs; prime calls simulate read-only; pack help and packages.md say package code runs on every plain check
where: docs/the-lock.md:94-103 (Executes repository code? table); yg prime line 144; cli/pack.ts:334; docs/packages.md:13-19; templates/knowledge/cli-reference.ts:1649
evidence: I put a marker-writing top-level statement into a check.mjs and a companion.mjs in $TMPDIR/consist-f. Commands that wrote no marker: `yg check`, `--no-approve`, `--approve --dry-run`, `context`, `impact`, `aspects --health`, `advise`, `structure`, `portal --static`, `aspects --json --reach`. That matches the table's "No" row. `yg simulate adv-rule --node cart` wrote the marker 4 times, through `aspect-test` subprocesses, and simulate is not in the table. Prime line 144 describes simulate as "Read-only, exits 0 whatever it finds". In the other direction, `yg pack --help` says "Installing a package runs its author's code on every check", and packages.md:14 says the script "runs in your process on every `yg check`". The table, and the fork-CI advice built on it ("run `yg check --no-approve`.
